subject: Re: Meditech RFP — Liability flowdown & software supply questionnaire
messages:
From: Megan Li <megan.li@meditech.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Meditech Procurement <procurement@meditech.com>, Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@qbrconsulting.com>
Date: 2026-10-29T13:02:00-07:00
Subject: Meditech RFP — Liability / flowdown questions

Dylan,

Thanks for taking our RFP. Attached is the liability and IP flowdown section we asked vendors to complete (Meditech_RFP_Liability_Questions.pdf). We need firm language on: indemnity carve-outs for third-party claims related to model outputs, liability caps tied to annual subscription vs. per-request costs, and whether Redwood flows down obligations to subcontractors (hosting, inference infra).

Specific asks:
- Can Redwood accept a total liability cap of the greater of USD 5M or 12 months of fees?
- Will Redwood provide IP indemnity for customer data processed by hosted inference?
- Do you have standard contract language for flowdown to cloud partners and any limitations?

Please respond with a document we can attach to the RFP pack, and flag any clauses you cannot accept so we can route to procurement counsel. Timeline: we'd like initial responses by COB 2026-10-30.

Regards,
Megan Li
Senior Procurement Manager
Meditech Health
Attachment: Meditech_RFP_Liability_Questions.pdf

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Megan Li <megan.li@meditech.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Meditech Procurement <procurement@meditech.com>
Date: 2026-10-30T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Meditech RFP — Liability / flowdown questions

Hi Megan — thanks for the clear ask and the deadline.

Attached is our initial pass that addresses each question with the current company standard positions (Redwood_Response_Liability_20261030.docx). High level:
- Liability cap: our standard public-facing cap is the greater of USD 3M or 12 months of fees. We can escalate to 5M for enterprise contracts with an approved committed spend profile; need procurement signal on committed ARR/term.
- IP indemnity: we indemnify against third-party IP claims alleging Redwood’s models or code infringe third-party IP. For customer data, we do not provide an indemnity tied to how customers use generated outputs (we offer strong contractual protections on data handling and the option for Private deployment for sensitive data).
- Flowdown to subcontractors: we require flowdown obligations for security and data handling. For liability, our agreements limit downstream flowdown to the extent required by law and typical commercial carve-outs for cloud providers.

I copied Aditya and Laura for legal and commercial confirmation on the caps and indemnity language — Laura, can you review and suggest specific redlines where necessary?

Next steps: Laura/Aditya — can you review the attached doc and flag must-change items by 2026-11-01 so we can issue a redline back to Meditech? Megan — expect a redline from us by early next week if we need to escalate.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
Attachment: Redwood_Response_Liability_20261030.docx

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T09:08:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Meditech RFP — Liability / flowdown questions (please advise)

Forwarding Meditech's liability questions and my initial draft. Quick summary of commercial levers:
- Raise cap to USD 5M if customer commits to a 36-month reserved/dedicated arrangement or commits > $X ARR (we should quantify).
- Consider a per-claim carve-out for third-party model hallucination losses — propose carve-out to be limited to consequential damages tied to business interruption rather than direct losses.

Inline:
> Megan asked whether we will "flow down obligations to subcontractors (hosting, inference infra)."

We currently have strong PSAs with our cloud partners (flowdown for security and incident response). For liability, we typically do not flow down full indemnity beyond what is contractually required. If Meditech insists, we can offer limited flowdown that mirrors our security obligations but not extend our indemnity to the cloud provider beyond their standard TOS.

Please mark items you want changed in the attached and call out any revenue threshold for increasing the cap to 5M. Also flag whether we should proactively offer Private deployment as an alternative to broaden acceptance of our standard positions.

Thanks — Dylan

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T11:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Meditech RFP — Liability / flowdown questions (commercial/legal notes)

Dylan — good capture. A few suggested positions:

1) Cap escalation: we can push to USD 5M if customer signs a 3-year dedicated capacity deal with a minimum committed monthly spend of $45k (approx. $1.6M ARR). If they want the 5M without committed spend, require additional price premium and an exceptions committee sign-off.

2) IP indemnity: keep our current indemnity language for third-party IP. For outputs, propose a limited warranty that generated content is provided "as-is" and the customer retains responsibility for downstream use. We should avoid a broad indemnity tied to customer use of outputs.

3) Flowdown: acceptable to provide flowdown for security/data handling; for liability/indemnity, limit to the extent required by vendor contracts. Add a clause that we will "use reasonable efforts" to obtain contractual commitments from subcontractors where commercially feasible.

4) Offer Private deployment: recommend we propose Private deployment for regulated PHI workloads — this materially reduces risk and is something Meditech values. It can be presented as a commercial alternative rather than changing our standard legal posture.

Laura — can you prepare the redline with the following: add the commercial threshold for cap escalation, tighten indemnity language around outputs, and include the flowdown "reasonable efforts" clause. If legal is comfortable, crisp language on data processing and KMS/HSM custody options.

-Aditya

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Megan Li <megan.li@meditech.com>, Meditech Procurement <procurement@meditech.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-02T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Meditech RFP — Liability / flowdown questions (Redwood redline enclosed)

Megan — thanks for your patience. Please find our edited redline of the Master Service Agreement and a short response memo attached (Redlines_Redwood_Master_Service_Agreement_20261102.pdf). Key points summarized:

- Liability cap: Redwood's baseline cap remains the greater of USD 3M or 12 months' fees. We will agree to a USD 5M cap when the customer: (a) executes a 36-month dedicated capacity agreement; and (b) commits to minimum monthly billing of USD 45k. We documented this as an optional clause the parties can elect.

- IP indemnity / outputs: Redwood will continue to indemnify for third-party IP claims alleging the service or Redwood-delivered software infringes third-party IP. We will not indemnify customers for losses resulting from customer use of model outputs. Instead, we provide robust data handling guarantees and the Private deployment option for high-risk data.

- Flowdown to subcontractors: we have inserted a "reasonable efforts" flowdown clause. We will flow down security/data handling obligations to subcontractors where contractually feasible; liability flowdown limited to statutory requirements and the subcontractor's standard indemnity limitations.

- Alternative: we propose inclusion of a Private deployment schedule (exhibit) as an accepted mitigation path for regulated workloads — this is included as an attachment to the redline.

If the above is acceptable, Dylan — please send the redline packet and short memo to Megan and procurement and confirm whether Meditech wants to proceed with the dedicated-cap pricing trigger or discuss alternatives.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Head of Legal — Contracts & Commercial
Redwood Inference
Attachment: Redlines_Redwood_Master_Service_Agreement_20261102.pdf
